help.title: Accepted attribute names
help.intro: Each feature in the file is a farm: its geometry (polygon or point) comes from the file and its data from these attributes, in upper or lower case. If your file doesn't carry the data, attach the production Excel to it and they are joined by ID.
help.notes: The Excel template's headers and the EUDR names (ProducerName, Area) are accepted too, so a GeoJSON downloaded from Monbo can be uploaded again as it is. In KML/KMZ, without an id the placemark's name is used. The Shapefile goes in a .zip with its .prj and can carry polygons and points as two Shapefiles.

farmsUpload.intro: You can use any of these options, whichever fits your data best. You can combine them: all the farms add up in the list below.
farmsUpload.dropzoneText: or drag and drop your files here
farmsUpload.joinedWith: Data from the Excel {{name}}, joined by ID
farmsUpload.excelWithoutCoordinates: This Excel has no coordinates. If your farms are in a geo file, upload it with this Excel in “Geo file + Excel”; if not, fill in its coordinate columns.
farmsUpload.excelWithCoordinates_one: This Excel has coordinates in 1 row. With a geo file, each farm is placed by the file: use the “Geo file + Excel” template, which has no coordinates, or delete the Excel's. If the Excel's coordinates are the right ones, upload it alone in “Excel template”.
farmsUpload.excelWithCoordinates_other: This Excel has coordinates in {{count}} rows. With a geo file, each farm is placed by the file: use the “Geo file + Excel” template, which has no coordinates, or delete the Excel's. If the Excel's coordinates are the right ones, upload it alone in “Excel template”.

excel.title: Excel template
excel.when: You have each farm's coordinates as text (WKT or GeoJSON).

steps.2: Fill in one row per farm, with its coordinates

excel.wrongType: This is for the Excel template. Geo files (GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, Shapefile) go in “Geo file with data” or in “Geo file + Excel”.

geoData.title: Geo file with data
geoData.when: Your farms are in a geo file (GeoJSON, KML/KMZ or Shapefile) that carries their data: producer, date, quantity, unit and crop.

steps.1: Check that the farms' attributes have the accepted names
steps.2: Upload the geo file (a Shapefile, in a .zip with its .prj)

geoData.wrongType: This is for a geo file. The Excel template goes in “Excel template”, or in “Geo file + Excel” with its geo file.

geoExcel.title: Geo file + Excel
geoExcel.when: Your farms are in a geo file (GeoJSON, KML/KMZ or Shapefile), for example from Google Earth, and their data in an Excel. They are joined by each farm's ID.

steps.1: Give each farm in the geo file its ID (in Google Earth, as its name)
steps.2: Fill in this option's template with the same IDs
steps.3: Upload the geo file and the Excel

geoExcel.wrongGeoType: This is for the geo file (GeoJSON, KML, KMZ or Shapefile). The production Excel goes next to it.
geoExcel.wrongExcelType: This is for the production Excel. The geo file goes next to it.
